info.title: Rat Things API
info.description: Open-source, self-hosted backend for cloud agents. Each deployment owns identity, OAuth applications, credentials, and data.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Optional unauthenticated routes that authenticate provider signatures before parsing.

200.description: Machine-readable deployment capabilities, agent guidance, and contract links
Create immutable Thing version v1 JSON Schema
Trusted plugin manifests, authentication fields, and operation schemas
Owner-scoped account metadata and grants; never credentials

201.description: Credential verified; derived connection metadata, secret binding, and initial grant created

200.description: Credential replaced in the host vault
Owner-scoped message and file matches across durable conversations
Safe conversation state and one cursor-paged durable transcript window
Updated durable pin, visibility, and read state
Mailbox, conversation, session, and bound run state
Current durable file catalog without S3 coordinates

302.description: Owner-checked redirect to short-lived private content

202.description: One durable Run accepted immediately. A thread only adds continuity preparation before dispatch.

200.description: Ordered typed live activity and pending input requests; raw App Server protocol data remains private

202.description: JSON result returned to App Server

200.description: Run file catalog without S3 coordinates

302.description: Publication redirect with host-only signed cookies

200.description: Thing lifecycle with explicit draft and published revisions
Compiled run request and diagnostics without credentials

202.description: Draft test run queued with exact revision evidence

200.description: The exact successfully tested draft revision was published and its trigger synchronized

awsSigV4.name: Authorization
awsSigV4.description: AWS Signature Version 4 for the reference deployment's execute-api routes. Host backends may wrap this endpoint and preserve a trusted principal.

Location.description: Relative owner-checked resource to poll or retrieve.

PublicConversationId.name: conversationId
PublicConversationId.description: Opaque owner-scoped ID returned by the conversation list.

Artifact.name: artifact
Artifact.description: Opaque artifact ID from the corresponding catalog endpoint.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Recommended for every submission and required when thread is present; reuse it to receive the same Run.

Credential.description: Provider credential fields written directly to the deployment's secret vault. Values are never returned by the API.

url.description: Credential-free HTTPS URL on a deployment-allowed host.

credentialSecretArn.description: Advanced host-side Secrets Manager binding; never embedded credentials.

RunSubmission.description: The universal Run submission. Optional thread continuity changes preparation, never the receipt or lifecycle.

thread.description: Optional owner-scoped continuity. Requires Idempotency-Key and still creates this request's Run immediately.

attachments.description: Files become encrypted durable conversation artifacts and are restored into replacement MicroVMs.

request.description: Must not use parentRunId or a source destination; use a Thing for new automation definitions.

title.description: Stable bounded title, normally derived from the first user message.

threadKey.description: Present only for API-created threads so an owner can submit a continuation.

hidden.description: Owner-scoped durable hidden state; hiding does not stop execution.

unread.description: True when the conversation changed after its durable read marker.

nextToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next older transcript window.

Run.description: Owner-visible run projection. Internal ownership keys, object-store coordinates, execution handles, conversation bindings, agent thread IDs, and provenance are available only to trusted orchestration.

ArtifactDescriptor.description: Owner-checked artifact metadata plus a time-bounded bearer URL. Legacy input/output/events/patch descriptors can use name instead of catalog fields.

RunReceipt.description: The queued run record. Consumers may follow the Location header for current state.
